transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today? Is there something specific that’s been troubling you?

I came in because my concentration has gotten unreliable. I’ll be at the clinic reviewing a chart, or even at home working on a watercolor, and I suddenly realize I’ve read the same line over and over. My mind just drifts to everything that could go wrong, and it’s starting to get in the way.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Yes. I do worry even when there isn’t anything right in front of me that needs fixing. My mind keeps going around things like whether my old patients are being cared for properly, whether the practice handoff is going to work out financially, and whether I’ll be useless once I’m fully retired. Even to me, it feels bigger than it should.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the worry and difficulty concentrating?
It’s been about a year and three months now. It started around when I began the formal process of retiring, and it’s just kind of kept going since then.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or fatigue, that seem to go along with these worries?

Yes, mainly fatigue. By the middle of the afternoon I feel pretty worn out, more than I used to. It’s not the kind of tired that a nap or a quiet morning really fixes. Even simple things like weeding the garden or standing at the easel to paint feel heavier than they should.
Have you found yourself feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, like your watercolor painting or other hobbies?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear loss of interest exactly. Some days I don’t get around to painting or hobbies as much, but I can’t say I feel completely uninterested in them.
Have you had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early more days than not?

Yes. Most nights I’m tired when I get into bed, but once it’s quiet I start going over things in my head—patient transfers, money details, that sort of thing. I do fall asleep eventually, but I’m often awake around four or five, and it feels like I never really settled into sleep.
Have you noticed feeling down or having a low mood that seems to stick around most of the day, even when there’s no clear reason for it?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get worn down and frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel low most of the day for no clear reason. It doesn’t really seem like that.
Do you find that your worrying feels uncontrollable, like you can’t stop thinking about these things even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes, it does feel that way. I’ll try to talk myself down, like I would with a nervous patient, and tell myself it’s probably fine. But then one worry turns into the next, and before I know it I’m checking emails, looking over notes, or asking the same thing again instead of just letting it go.
Have you noticed any days where you don’t take pleasure or feel enjoyment from things that usually make you happy, like your painting or time with loved ones?
I can’t say I’ve really noticed that. I still enjoy those things when I’m doing them. Maybe I’m distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say the enjoyment is gone.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not living up to your own expectations, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Not really, no. I mean, I have high standards for myself, and I can get annoyed if I think I should’ve handled something better. But I wouldn’t say I feel guilty for no clear reason or like I’m failing somehow.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I haven’t really noticed moving slower, no. Restless… maybe a little fidgety at times, but I wouldn’t say I’m unable to sit still in any obvious way.
Have you ever felt guilty about things that, in hindsight, you couldn’t really control or shouldn’t be responsible for?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can second-guess myself sometimes, but feeling guilty about things I truly couldn’t control… no, that doesn’t really sound like me.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or increased fatigue even when you haven't been doing much physically or mentally?

Yes, I have noticed that. By midafternoon I can feel pretty worn out, even if the day hasn’t been especially physical. It’s not the kind of tired that a quiet morning or a quick nap really fixes. Even simple things, like weeding the garden or standing at the easel, feel heavier than they used to.
Have you noticed that your ability to think clearly or make decisions has gotten worse, or that you often feel indecisive about even small things?

Yes, that’s actually a big part of why I came in. My concentration has gotten pretty unreliable. I’ll be reviewing a chart at the clinic, or even laying out a watercolor wash, and suddenly I realize I’ve read the same line three times because my mind has gone off to everything that could go wrong. Decisions are harder mostly because I can’t stay focused on the thing in front of me.
Have you noticed any days where you don’t take pleasure or feel enjoyment from things that usually make you happy, like your painting or time with loved ones?

I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost pleasure in them. I still enjoy painting and being with my family when I’m actually doing those things. Maybe I’m a little distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say the enjoyment is gone.
Have you had days where you feel down or sad most of the time, even when nothing particularly bad has happened?
No, not really. I mean, I get worried and worn out, but I wouldn’t say I feel down or sad most of the day for no clear reason. That hasn’t been the main thing I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed that you’re more agitated or fidgety lately, even if you’re not aware of feeling anxious or worried?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself being especially fidgety or agitated out of nowhere. If it’s happening, it hasn’t stood out to me.
Do you find that you worry excessively about a number of different events or activities, more days than not, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Yes. I do. My mind just keeps going around and around on a lot of things—whether my old patients are being looked after properly, whether the handoff of the practice is going to work out financially, and whether I’m going to become kind of useless once I’m fully retired. Even to me, it feels like the amount of worry is more than the situation really calls for.
Have you noticed that you're fidgeting, pacing, or unable to sit still more often than usual, even when you're not trying to do anything active?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself pacing or being unable to sit still more than usual. If anything, I’m just sort of tense, but not up and moving around in a way that stands out.
